name: Server host
author: marshmallow-mia
summary: Host an Echo VR game server from your launcher's install: writes the server's own setup (its account, EchoVRCE or another Nakama, its region, and the mods the Mods page has on, EchoCombat too) and gives you the command that starts it.

write.otherwise: This plugin needs a newer launcher: Settings, Update now.
Fill in the server account's Discord ID first.
Fill in the server account's password first.

columns.title: Your game server
columns.help: The account your server signs in with on EchoVRCE (or another Nakama below), not your own player account.

blocks.text: This plugin needs a newer launcher: Settings, Update now.

blocks.label: Password
blocks.hint: The server account's: it's kept in plain text, in the server's own folder

blocks.label: Region
blocks.hint: Where it registers, e.g. uwu. Several: comma-separated

blocks.label: Guilds
blocks.hint: Optional: the guild ids it hosts for, comma-separated. Each guild has to give the server account its server host role

blocks.label: Port
blocks.hint: Forward it (UDP and TCP) to this PC: EchoVRCE checks it when the server registers

blocks.text: Run it whenever you want the server up (Windows: double-click start-server in its setup folder, or run the command in a Command Prompt). nEVR ends a server after each match, and the script starts it again. To stop it on Windows, close the server's window, then press S in the script's; on Linux, Ctrl+C. Write the setup again after changing mods on the Mods page.

columns.title: Services
columns.help: EchoVRCE's, unless your server plays on another Nakama.

blocks.label: Folder
blocks.hint: In the game's _local folder: one per server setup

blocks.text: Write the server setup puts the server's own config.yaml and config.json into the live build's _local folder. They hold the account and services above, and the mods the Mods page has on, a content pack such as EchoCombat included.

Its start script runs echovr.exe as a headless server on that setup (-config-path), and again after each match. PLAY and the launcher never change it, and the server signs in as its own account, not as yours. On Linux it runs in a Wine prefix of its own, so you can play beside it.
A content pack on a server needs nEVR 4.1.0 or newer (the launcher's game update).
